newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firmer after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firmer after quiet day.

text.p: IPE July gas oil ended an uneventful day's trade just 25 cents off the opening price after trading in a narrow range.
The prompt July contract closed up $1.50 at $162.75 a tonne, gains made mainly on the back of a late rise on Brent on Monday.
The July/Aug gas oil spread was well bid at 75 cents in contango.
"The front spread held up well and is well bid," one broker said.
August Brent gained some ground on the back of firmer NYMEX unleaded gasoline and had notched up 14 cents to $18.33 a barrel by 1700 GMT.
Traders said the market was waiting for weekly U.S. statistics from the American Petroleum Institute due out after markets close on Tuesday.

"If there is nothing to support prices, there we could be in for another fall," one said, adding that the North Sea crude market was well supported for the rest of the week with few barrels remaining from the July programme after active trade on Tuesday.
Traders were on the alert for further news on the timing of the next Iraqi exports.
"Everyone expects Iraqi crude soon but I think there is further (price) downside on the back of the headline that says it (crude) really is coming," one North Sea trader said.
The U.N. coordinator in Baghdad said earlier he hoped the world body would receive by 2000 GMT Iraq's food distribution plan under the oil-for-food deal.
